# Polyglot Codebase Knowledge Graph

> Generated offline by **readmenator**. 289 files, 7449 symbols, 1674 imports. Supports C, C++, Python, Go, Rust, JS/TS, Java, C#, Shell, PHP, Dart, GDScript, Nim, ASM, Ruby, Swift, Kotlin, Scala, Lua, Elixir.
> No LLMs. No tokens. Pure static analysis. See more [here](https://github.com/grisuno/ReadMenator)

**Start here:** Statistics Dashboard for scope, God Nodes for blast radius, Architecture Reference for per-file API. Agents: prefer `readmenator-agent/INDEX.md` + `SYMBOLS.md`.

**Wiki:** prefer `readmenator-wiki/index.md` for progressive disclosure: one synthesis page per community, `connections.json` with EXTRACTED vs INFERRED confidence, `queries.md` log, `REPORT.md` audit.

**Confidence:** EXTRACTED = parsed from source, INFERRED = heuristic bridge, AMBIGUOUS = reported, never hidden. See `readmenator-wiki/REPORT.md`.

## Query Recipes

Example queries you can run against this knowledge base using the ranking engine:

```
# Find files most relevant to a concept
readmenator query "Where is the import resolver implemented?"

# Rank files by relevance to a topic
readmenator query "How does documentation generation work?"

# Explain why a file ranks highly
readmenator query "explain readmenator/_documentation.py"

# Trace dependency paths with ranked context
readmenator query "path from CLI to exporter"
```

The ranking model uses the following signals:

- **Personalized PageRank** (45% weight): query-specific relevance via seed propagation
- **Global Authority** (20% weight): structural importance via standard PageRank
- **Test Coverage** (15% weight): fraction of symbols referenced in test files
- **Doc Coverage** (10% weight): presence of docstrings and file-level docs
- **Freshness** (10% weight): recent modification activity

Results include score decomposition and justification paths for each ranked item.

Matching by URL content instead is stable across a doc rebuild with no re-fetch needed (the decoded surface is reused as-is): a JS timer firing seconds into a page like an ad-heavy anime-streaming * site is exactly the case this fixes.", "kind": "struct", "line": 260, "name": "ui_image"}, {"doc": "A decoded CSS background-image for one box of the current doc (2026-07-16). A blocklist entry blocks a domain and all its subdomains; an allowlist entry re-enables a domain and its subdomains, so a single subdomain can be seen even when its parent domain is blocked. The allowlist wins over the blocklist.  This is an adblock-style filter, not the security boundary (that is the sandbox and the network policy): on any doubt it fails OPEN (does not over-block), since silently dropping content is worse here than letting one tracker through.  See spec/hostblock.md for the full contract.", "kind": "type_alias", "line": 29, "name": "hb_set", "signature": "typedef struct hb_set hb_set;"}, {"doc": "} hb_list; typedef enum hb_decision { HB_ALLOW = 0,  /* the host may be contacted HB_BLOCK       /* the host is on the blocklist (and not re-enabled) } hb_decision; typedef enum hb_status { HB_OK = 0, HB_ERR_NULL_ARG,  /* set or text was NULL HB_ERR_OOM        /* allocation failure while growing a table } hb_status; /* Allocates an empty set. The parameters are per-container, not per-run: carrying them on every run of a container was pure duplication across the IPC.  parent_id is the id of the enclosing container (-1 = top level) and parent_item is THIS container's item ordinal within that parent, so a nested container is one item * of its parent. A compositor queues events for a client in a small buffer (4 KiB) backed by the socket; a client that does not read for a few seconds while the pointer moves gets DISCONNECTED (\"libwayland: Data too big for buffer ... error in client communication\"). Freedom blocks its GUI thread on page loads, image fetches and big layouts, so a helper thread reads the socket meanwhile. It uses libwayland's documented multi-thread pattern: wl_display_prepare_read_queue on a PRIVATE (always empty) queue, so the events are only enqueued -- every handler still runs on the GUI thread, in order, when the main loop dispatches. Exercises the headless image pipeline end-to-end (render_doc_images -> load_images -> local disk read -> worker decode -> Cairo surface -> free_images); under `make asan` the asan-instrumented freedom subprocess turns any leak/UAF in that path into a failure here. The declared 120x80 clears the tracking-pixel gate so the image is ALLOWed and * actually decoded; the visual-review PNG confirms the pixels (see CLAUDE.md).", "kind": "function", "line": 819, "name": "test_download_png_images_local", "signature": "static void test_download_png_images_local(void **state)"}, {"doc": "char args[512]; assert_true((size_t)snprintf(args, sizeof args, \"--images --download-png=%s %s\", png, html_path) < sizeof args); int rc = -1; assert_int_equal(run_freedom_raw(args, &rc), 0); assert_int_equal(rc, 0); assert_true(is_png_file(png)); /* real bitmap, image decoded (not a placeholder-only render) unlink(img); unlink(html_path); unlink(png); } /* --download-png with no PATH is a usage error (fail closed: never guess a path).", "kind": "function", "line": 880, "name": "test_download_png_requires_path", "signature": "static void test_download_png_requires_path(void **state)"}, {"doc": "Regression for the M1.1-adjacent paint-order fix in write_doc_png/paint_structured (gui/browser_ui.c, paint_positioned_one): CSS 2.1 Appendix E puts a negative z-index stacking context in a paint-order layer that precedes in-flow content, so it must paint BEHIND, not on top of, an overlapping in-flow box. Before the fix, Stage 2's two passes both ran after the in-flow paint, so #front (in-flow, blue, no explicit position) never covered #behind (position:absolute; z-index:-1; red) even though #behind is meant to sit underneath it -- the sampled pixel came back pure red. Decodes the exported PNG (via image_decode, the project's own PNG * decoder) and asserts the overlap pixel is blue, not red.", "kind": "function", "line": 896, "name": "test_download_png_negative_zindex_paints_behind_inflow", "signature": "static void test_download_png_negative_zindex_paints_behind_inflow(void **state)"}, {"doc": "An absolutely positioned box with overflow:hidden clips its OWN content (CSS Overflow 3 2.2). The visually-hidden idiom (`.sr-only{position:absolute;width:1px; height:1px;overflow:hidden}`, on nearly every modern site) painted its whole label over the page -- lobste.rs' \"Lobsters\" over its logo. A dark label is placed in a * 1x1 hidden box on a white page: no ink may reach the area it would cover.", "kind": "function", "line": 1000, "name": "test_download_png_positioned_overflow_clips_own_content", "signature": "static void test_download_png_positioned_overflow_clips_own_content(void **state)"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 1048, "name": "blend", "signature": "* not some other blend (double-composited or wrong alpha). */\nstatic void test_download_png_group..."}, {"doc": "An out-of-flow box with `width: auto` SHRINK-WRAPS to its content (CSS 2.2 §10.3.7) instead of filling its containing block, and a `position:relative` wrapper that holds only out-of-flow children still generates its own box (so it paints and acts as their containing block).  Both used to be wrong together: the wrapper registered no box at all (its only children were out of flow, so nothing in the flow referenced it), which left the absolutes resolving against a degenerate 0x0 containing block; and auto width fell back to the FULL content width, so a right-anchored badge was placed at cb_right - full_width, i.e. far off the left edge of the page. parity` leaves behind into something you can act on.  `make parity` prints one score per page. To fix a page you then need to SEE where the two engines part ways. This reads build/parity/<name>.fd.png (Freedom) and <name>.ff.png (Firefox) and, per page: * writes build/bench/<name>.sbs.png: Freedom | Firefox side by side, cropped to the band you ask for, so one Read shows the difference; * prints the first row where the pictures diverge and the worst 100 px bands by mean luminance difference, so you know which y to crop next; * ranks the pages by score and shows the delta against tests/parity/baseline.tsv.  Every page the README shows (README_PAGES) is also republished: its docs/img/compare-*.png is rewritten from the fresh pair and its score in the README table is updated, so the README always carries the latest render. --no-readme skips that.  Render time is measured too (spec/parity.md \"Timing\"): for the README pages -- or the pages named -- the REAL GUI window (tools/guitime.py: Xvfb + weston, same do_load/paint path as a user) and Firefox (tools/fftime.py: its own Performance Timeline) each report \"navigation request -> painted and idle\"; the medians are printed with the ratio and the delta against tests/parity/timing-baseline.tsv, saved to build/bench/timing.tsv, and written into the README between its fbench-timing markers. If the GUI cannot be run here (no Xvfb/weston) that is said and nothing is substituted. --no-time skips it.  Usage: fbench.py [--from Y] [--rows N] [--band PX] [--no-readme] [--no-time] [--time-runs N] [page ...] no page  -> every page that has a PNG pair (timing: the README pages) Run `make fbench PAGES=\"a b\" FROM=1000 ROWS=800` to refresh the pair first.", "id": "tools/fbench.py", "kind": "module", "label": "fbench.py", "language": "py", "sha256": "ff4a0be532128f3b", "symbol_count": 11, "symbols": [{"kind": "function", "line": 53, "name": "load_baseline", "signature": "def load_baseline()"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 66, "name": "load_current", "signature": "def load_current()"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 79, "name": "luma", "signature": "def luma(img)"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 83, "name": "bands", "signature": "def bands(fd, ff, band)"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 95, "name": "sbs", "signature": "def sbs(name, start, nrows)"}, {"doc": "Rewrite the README picture of `name` and the score printed beside its label.", "kind": "function", "line": 114, "name": "publish_readme", "signature": "def publish_readme(name, score)"}, {"doc": "Runs a timing tool over the pages; returns ({name: median ms}, exit code).", "kind": "function", "line": 140, "name": "run_timer", "signature": "def run_timer(tool, pages, runs)"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 158, "name": "load_timing_baseline", "signature": "def load_timing_baseline()"}, {"doc": "Rewrites the README timing table (between the markers) for the README pages timed.", "kind": "function", "line": 171, "name": "publish_timing", "signature": "def publish_timing(rows)"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 193, "name": "timing", "signature": "def timing(names, runs, readme)"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 227, "name": "main", "signature": "def main()"}]}, {"doc": "ffgeom -- Firefox geometry as TEXT, no image reading.  The `make geom` loop needs Firefox's getBoundingClientRect() numbers, and its only headless output here is a screenshot. This tool turns that screenshot into a text dump mechanically: the probe page replaces the body with a BIT-GRID canvas that encodes every measured rect as black/white cells, this script decodes the cells back into numbers, and prints one line per rect:  <index> <tag>.<class> top=<t> left=<l> w=<w> h=<h>  The encoding is a fixed grid, no OCR, no image model: - canvas 64px wide, each row 16 cells of 4x4px, one row per 16-bit VALUE - row 0: magic 0xC0DE (16 bits) + row count (16 bits) - then per rect: 4 rows (top, left, w, h), MSB first - rows continue per rect; the decoded count bounds the region read  The decoded values are what `make geom` prints beside Freedom's own --dump-layout, so a layout difference reads as two columns of numbers instead of being guessed from pixels. The canvas is white and fixed at the top-left of the viewport, so the grid region carries no underlying page ink.  Usage: ffgeom probe <page.html> <selector> <out.html> ffgeom decode <screenshot.png>  Both steps run through `make geom` (the Makefile is the single source of truth); this script is the thin worker it delegates to. Pure python, no dependencies, no network. It reads only local files the harness produced.", "id": "tools/ffgeom.py", "kind": "module", "label": "ffgeom.py", "language": "py", "sha256": "ce4ee286c90716b7", "symbol_count": 12, "symbols": [{"kind": "function", "line": 116, "name": "load_rows", "signature": "def load_rows(path)"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 169, "name": "lum", "signature": "def lum(p)"}, {"doc": "Loads a probe screenshot and returns a function reading 16-bit words from\nthe bit-grid at (x0, y0). Shared by `decode` (rects) and `height` (the page's\nreal scrollHeight).", "kind": "function", "line": 173, "name": "_word_reader", "signature": "def _word_reader(path)"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 239, "name": "decode", "signature": "def decode(path)"}, {"doc": "Inserts the probe script before </body> (else </html>, else at EOF: many\nWPT files omit the explicit body close and the parser closes it for us).", "kind": "function", "line": 254, "name": "_append_probe", "signature": "def _append_probe(src, script)"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 265, "name": "probe", "signature": "def probe(page, selector, out_html)"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 279, "name": "height_probe", "signature": "def height_probe(page, out_html)"}, {"doc": "Decodes the scrollHeight carried by the #__ffh sentinel: the probe encodes\none rect (its height), which decode() returns as the first element's h value.", "kind": "function", "line": 292, "name": "height", "signature": "def height(path)"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 301, "name": "main", "signature": "def main(argv)"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 181, "name": "lum_at", "signature": "def lum_at(x, y)"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 206, "name": "bit", "signature": "def bit(grid_row, cell, origin)"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 209, "name": "word", "signature": "def word(grid_row, origin)"}]}, {"doc": "ffq -- ask Firefox what it computed, as TEXT.  `make geom` prints Firefox's rects as an image; this tool prints them (and any computed property) as plain lines, so a layout difference is one grep away instead of a guess. The page loads with JavaScript OFF and the network dead, exactly like `make parity` (file:// stays reachable); the query itself runs through geckodriver, which executes outside the page's own script policy.  Usage: ffq.py <page.html> <css-selector> [prop ...] [--width N] [--height N] [--max N] Prints one line per match: <i> <tag>.<class> x=.. y=.. w=.. h=..  prop=value ... Coordinates are document coordinates (scroll included), integers.", "id": "tools/ffq.py", "kind": "module", "label": "ffq.py", "language": "py", "sha256": "3cb704d9d768e456", "symbol_count": 1, "symbols": [{"kind": "function", "line": 22, "name": "main", "signature": "def main()"}]}, {"doc": "ffshot -- full-page Firefox screenshot at a FIXED viewport, for `make parity`/`make wpt`.  `firefox --screenshot` sizes its viewport itself, so a page whose layout depends on `vh` (a hero of `min-height:100vh`, a sticky sidebar capped at `100vh`) rendered against a different viewport than Freedom's normalised 1080px one and scored as an engine bug. This drives the same Firefox through geckodriver with an explicit window size and asks for the full-page capture, so both engines see the same `vh`.  Same policy as the rest of the harness: JavaScript off and every network request sent to a dead proxy (file:// and data: stay reachable), because Freedom renders with JS off and blocks third parties by doctrine -- the reference has to measure the same document.  Usage: ffshot.py <page.html> <out.png> [width] [height] Exit 0 on success; any failure prints one line to stderr and exits 1.", "id": "tools/ffshot.py", "kind": "module", "label": "ffshot.py", "language": "py", "sha256": "3a99cc440cb43bd6", "symbol_count": 1, "symbols": [{"kind": "function", "line": 24, "name": "main", "signature": "def main()"}]}, {"doc": "fftime -- Firefox's time from \"navigate\" to \"painted and idle\", for `make fbench`.  Counterpart of the GUI's FREEDOM_GUI_TIMING (spec/parity.md \"Timing\"): the clock starts when the navigation is requested; the time is max(load event end, first painted frame) from the browser's own Performance Timeline (so it carries no WebDriver round trip). It is a LOWER bound of Firefox's true idle time (it cannot see later repaints such as image decode), which makes the comparison unfavourable to Freedom, never to Firefox. Same policy as the rest of the harness (JavaScript off, every network request sent to a dead proxy, file:// and data: reachable) and the same viewport as ffshot. One browser session serves every page; each page gets one untimed warm-up navigation (disk cache, font and layout caches, the way a returning user sees it) and RUNS timed ones; the median is reported.  Usage: fftime.py [--runs N] [--width W] [--height H] <page.html> ... Prints one line per page:  <name>\\t<median ms>\\t<min>\\t<max> Exit 0 when every page was measured; 1 on any failure (reported on stderr).", "id": "tools/fftime.py", "kind": "module", "label": "fftime.py", "language": "py", "sha256": "e1cf1e536489dfd2", "symbol_count": 1, "symbols": [{"kind": "function", "line": 38, "name": "main", "signature": "def main()"}]}, {"id": "tools/gen_psl.c", "kind": "module", "label": "gen_psl.c", "language": "c", "sha256": "325db63a103177ad", "symbol_count": 8, "symbols": [{"kind": "struct", "line": 21, "name": "vec"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 27, "name": "vec_push", "signature": "static void vec_push(vec *v, const char *s)"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 38, "name": "cmp_str", "signature": "static int cmp_str(const void *a, const void *b)"}, {"doc": "v->cap = v->cap ? v->cap * 2 : 1024; v->items = (char **)realloc(v->items, v->cap * sizeof *v->items); if (v->items == NULL) { fputs(\"oom\\n\", stderr); exit(1); } } v->items[v->len] = strdup(s); if (v->items[v->len] == NULL) { fputs(\"oom\\n\", stderr); exit(1); } v->len++; } static int cmp_str(const void *a, const void *b) { return strcmp(*(const char *const *)a, *(const char *const *)b); } /* Sorts then drops adjacent duplicates in place.", "kind": "function", "line": 43, "name": "sort_unique", "signature": "static void sort_unique(vec *v)"}, {"doc": "/* Sorts then drops adjacent duplicates in place. static void sort_unique(vec *v) { qsort(v->items, v->len, sizeof *v->items, cmp_str); size_t w = 0; for (size_t i = 0; i < v->len; ++i) { if (w == 0 || strcmp(v->items[w - 1], v->items[i]) != 0) { v->items[w++] = v->items[i]; } } v->len = w; } /* ASCII-lowercases in place; UTF-8 high bytes are left untouched.", "kind": "function", "line": 55, "name": "ascii_lower", "signature": "static void ascii_lower(char *s)"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 61, "name": "emit", "signature": "static void emit(const char *name, vec *v)"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 67, "name": "main", "signature": "int main(int argc, char **argv)"}, {"kind": "macro", "line": 15, "name": "_POSIX_C_SOURCE", "signature": "#define _POSIX_C_SOURCE"}]}, {"doc": "guitime -- how long the REAL Freedom window takes from \"navigate\" to \"painted and idle\".  Not headless: the browser is the GUI binary running in a nested weston (Xvfb + weston, pixman renderer), loading the page through the same do_load/render/paint path a user's session takes. The only addition is FREEDOM_GUI_TIMING=<file>: once the page is loaded, no background job or JS tick is pending and no new frame was painted for 150 ms, the window writes {\"ms\": <last paint - navigation request>} and exits (FREEDOM_GUI_EXIT_AT_IDLE). Nothing is timed in a separate mode (spec/parity.md).  The page is measured under the corpus policy (FREEDOM_AS_HOST=corpus.test with tests/parity/hosts: presentation trust, JavaScript off), the same one `make parity` and tools/fftime.py use. A scratch profile directory keeps the user's own preferences out of the measurement. If Xvfb or weston is missing the tool says so and exits 2: it never falls back to a different, headless measurement.  Usage: guitime.py [--runs N] [--bin PATH] [--hosts DIR] <page.html> ... - `ui_image` (line 260) - *href is an OWNED copy of the image's URL, not a pointer into w->doc (fixed 2026-07-16): a worker result applied outside a fresh navigation (a click, or a JS timer firing via OP_TICK -- see apply_click_result) rebuilds w->doc WHOLESALE from scratch without re-running load_images, so any rd_block* recorded here would immediately dangle and, worse, silently stop matching ANY block in the new doc (find_image compared pointer identity) -- every already-decoded image would revert to its placeholder on the very next repaint even though nothing about the image actually changed. Matching by URL content instead is stable across a doc rebuild with no re-fetch needed (the decoded surface is reused as-is): a JS timer firing seconds into a page like an ad-heavy anime-streaming * site is exactly the case this fixes.*

All owned pointers are transferred by value (no deep copy, no free): exactly one of {live window field, * inactive slot} owns each allocation at any time.*

**Enums:**
- `cx_layer` (line 27) - *allocation: given a box's already-resolved style scalars it decides (a) whether the box establishes a stacking context and (b) which of the seven paint-order layers it paints in, and gives a deterministic total order for painting a set of boxes. Like js_policy/webcaps it is decision logic over validated scalars, so it is directly testable and needs no fuzzing (it parses no remote content). The Cairo orchestration (offscreen layer surfaces, group opacity, blend) lives on the trusted side and consumes this module.  See spec/compositor.md.  /* Paint-order layers within one stacking context, back to front (CSS 2.1 App E).*

- `hb_set` (line 29) `typedef struct hb_set hb_set;` - *caller reads the list files and passes their text in; this module parses them into hash tables and decides whether a host is blocked. It opens no sockets and reads no files. The orchestrator consults hb_check() BEFORE opening a socket.  A blocklist entry blocks a domain and all its subdomains; an allowlist entry re-enables a domain and its subdomains, so a single subdomain can be seen even when its parent domain is blocked. The allowlist wins over the blocklist.  This is an adblock-style filter, not the security boundary (that is the sandbox and the network policy): on any doubt it fails OPEN (does not over-block), since silently dropping content is worse here than letting one tracker through. #### `fbench.py`
**Path:** `tools/fbench.py`
**File Doc:** *fbench -- turn the PNG pairs `make parity` leaves behind into something you can act on.  `make parity` prints one score per page. To fix a page you then need to SEE where the two engines part ways. This reads build/parity/<name>.fd.png (Freedom) and <name>.ff.png (Firefox) and, per page: * writes build/bench/<name>.sbs.png: Freedom | Firefox side by side, cropped to the band you ask for, so one Read shows the difference; * prints the first row where the pictures diverge and the worst 100 px bands by mean luminance difference, so you know which y to crop next; * ranks the pages by score and shows the delta against tests/parity/baseline.tsv.  Every page the README shows (README_PAGES) is also republished: its docs/img/compare-*.png is rewritten from the fresh pair and its score in the README table is updated, so the README always carries the latest render. --no-readme skips that.  Render time is measured too (spec/parity.md "Timing"): for the README pages -- or the pages named -- the REAL GUI window (tools/guitime.py: Xvfb + weston, same do_load/paint path as a user) and Firefox (tools/fftime.py: its own Performance Timeline) each report "navigation request -> painted and idle"; the medians are printed with the ratio and the delta against tests/parity/timing-baseline.tsv, saved to build/bench/timing.tsv, and written into the README between its fbench-timing markers. If the GUI cannot be run here (no Xvfb/weston) that is said and nothing is substituted. --no-time skips it.  Usage: fbench.py [--from Y] [--rows N] [--band PX] [--no-readme] [--no-time] [--time-runs N] [page ...] no page  -> every page that has a PNG pair (timing: the README pages) Run `make fbench PAGES="a b" FROM=1000 ROWS=800` to refresh the pair first.*

#### `ffgeom.py`
**Path:** `tools/ffgeom.py`
**File Doc:** *ffgeom -- Firefox geometry as TEXT, no image reading.  The `make geom` loop needs Firefox's getBoundingClientRect() numbers, and its only headless output here is a screenshot. This tool turns that screenshot into a text dump mechanically: the probe page replaces the body with a BIT-GRID canvas that encodes every measured rect as black/white cells, this script decodes the cells back into numbers, and prints one line per rect:  <index> <tag>.<class> top=<t> left=<l> w=<w> h=<h>  The encoding is a fixed grid, no OCR, no image model: - canvas 64px wide, each row 16 cells of 4x4px, one row per 16-bit VALUE - row 0: magic 0xC0DE (16 bits) + row count (16 bits) - then per rect: 4 rows (top, left, w, h), MSB first - rows continue per rect; the decoded count bounds the region read  The decoded values are what `make geom` prints beside Freedom's own --dump-layout, so a layout difference reads as two columns of numbers instead of being guessed from pixels. The canvas is white and fixed at the top-left of the viewport, so the grid region carries no underlying page ink.  Usage: ffgeom probe <page.html> <selector> <out.html> ffgeom decode <screenshot.png>  Both steps run through `make geom` (the Makefile is the single source of truth); this script is the thin worker it delegates to. Pure python, no dependencies, no network. It reads only local files the harness produced.*

#### `ffshot.py`
**Path:** `tools/ffshot.py`
**File Doc:** *ffshot -- full-page Firefox screenshot at a FIXED viewport, for `make parity`/`make wpt`.  `firefox --screenshot` sizes its viewport itself, so a page whose layout depends on `vh` (a hero of `min-height:100vh`, a sticky sidebar capped at `100vh`) rendered against a different viewport than Freedom's normalised 1080px one and scored as an engine bug. This drives the same Firefox through geckodriver with an explicit window size and asks for the full-page capture, so both engines see the same `vh`.  Same policy as the rest of the harness: JavaScript off and every network request sent to a dead proxy (file:// and data: stay reachable), because Freedom renders with JS off and blocks third parties by doctrine -- the reference has to measure the same document.  Usage: ffshot.py <page.html> <out.png> [width] [height] Exit 0 on success; any failure prints one line to stderr and exits 1.*

#### `fftime.py`
**Path:** `tools/fftime.py`
**File Doc:** *fftime -- Firefox's time from "navigate" to "painted and idle", for `make fbench`.  Counterpart of the GUI's FREEDOM_GUI_TIMING (spec/parity.md "Timing"): the clock starts when the navigation is requested; the time is max(load event end, first painted frame) from the browser's own Performance Timeline (so it carries no WebDriver round trip). It is a LOWER bound of Firefox's true idle time (it cannot see later repaints such as image decode), which makes the comparison unfavourable to Freedom, never to Firefox. Same policy as the rest of the harness (JavaScript off, every network request sent to a dead proxy, file:// and data: reachable) and the same viewport as ffshot. One browser session serves every page; each page gets one untimed warm-up navigation (disk cache, font and layout caches, the way a returning user sees it) and RUNS timed ones; the median is reported.  Usage: fftime.py [--runs N] [--width W] [--height H] <page.html> ... Prints one line per page:  <name>\t<median ms>\t<min>\t<max> Exit 0 when every page was measured; 1 on any failure (reported on stderr).*

#### `guitime.py`
**Path:** `tools/guitime.py`
**File Doc:** *guitime -- how long the REAL Freedom window takes from "navigate" to "painted and idle".  Not headless: the browser is the GUI binary running in a nested weston (Xvfb + weston, pixman renderer), loading the page through the same do_load/render/paint path a user's session takes. The only addition is FREEDOM_GUI_TIMING=<file>: once the page is loaded, no background job or JS tick is pending and no new frame was painted for 150 ms, the window writes {"ms": <last paint - navigation request>} and exits (FREEDOM_GUI_EXIT_AT_IDLE). Nothing is timed in a separate mode (spec/parity.md).  The page is measured under the corpus policy (FREEDOM_AS_HOST=corpus.test with tests/parity/hosts: presentation trust, JavaScript off), the same one `make parity` and tools/fftime.py use. A scratch profile directory keeps the user's own preferences out of the measurement. If Xvfb or weston is missing the tool says so and exits 2: it never falls back to a different, headless measurement.  Usage: guitime.py [--runs N] [--bin PATH] [--hosts DIR] <page.html> ... Prints one line per page:  <name>\t<median ms>\t<min>\t<max> Exit 0 when every page was measured, 1 on a failed measurement, 2 when the environment is missing.*

#### `mutate.py`
**Path:** `tools/mutate.py`
**File Doc:** *mutate -- compile-time mutation testing for the CMocka suites.  One mutant = one operator substitution in one src/ file that has a matching tests/test_<module>.c. The mutated source replaces the original for a single `make build/test_<module>` build and run, then the original is restored.  killed          the suite ran and at least one test failed survived        the suite passed on the mutated code (a blind spot) killed-by-build the mutation broke -Werror or the link (reported apart, because a syntax error is not the suite's work)  Exit status: 0 when every mutant died, 1 when any mutant survived.  The mutation set is deliberately mechanical (comparison/relational/logical/ arithmetic operators): each is one token swap on a line of the module's own code, never inside comments or strings. Only the first MUTATE_MAX sites per file are taken, in line order, so the run stays bounded.  Usage: tools/mutate.py [--max N] [--mods a,b,c] [--verbose]*

#### `pngprof.py`
**Path:** `tools/pngprof.py`
**File Doc:** *pngprof -- structural ink-profile dump for page screenshots.  Build-time tool for Freedom layout work (companion to tools/pngdiff.c). Where pngdiff reduces two renders to one scalar score, pngprof prints WHERE the ink sits: the horizontal column profile split into vertical bands, and the cumulative vertical ink distribution. That is what turns a divergence like "slashdot col_mae 0.39" into a statement like "the article column spans x=120..600 in Firefox but x=0..950 in Freedom".  It answers the questions an agent cannot answer by looking at the PNG: with no image input available (or when the numbers matter more than the picture), the agent reads these profiles instead. Ink is defined against the image's modal background luminance, exactly like pngdiff, so a dark author theme and a forced light theme compare meaningfully.  Decoder: pure python (zlib + the five PNG filters), no third-party packages, so it runs anywhere the repo runs. RGBA/RGB/grey/16-bit screenshots all normalise to an 8-bit RGB row buffer. It reads only local files that the harness or the operator just produced; it never sees remote content and is not part of the browser's attack surface.  Usage: pngprof <image.png> [--bands N] [--cols C] [--rows R]  Output (stdout): - image width/height and the background luminance used - the column profile: C buckets, each printed as the ink fraction of that bucket's cells, repeated per vertical band*

#### `prune.py`
**Path:** `tools/prune.py`
**File Doc:** *prune -- cut a corpus page down to ONE subtree, keeping its whole ancestor chain.  Isolating a layout bug on a 400 KB page by eye is slow; isolating it by deleting everything that is not on the path to the element is mechanical. The <head> (every <style> and <link>) is kept as is, so the cascade is untouched; in the <body> only the target subtree and its ancestors survive, with every other sibling dropped along the path. Scripts are removed (both engines render with JS off anyway).  Usage: prune.py <page.html> <xpath> <out.html> xpath  selects the element(s) to keep, e.g. '//nav[@class="nav-primary"]' Prints the number of matched elements; exits 1 when none matched.*

#### `snapshot.py`
**Path:** `tools/snapshot.py`
**File Doc:** *Freeze a live page into one self-contained HTML file for `make parity`.  Both engines must render the SAME document offline (spec/parity.md), so every same-site <link rel=stylesheet> is fetched once and inlined as <style>, and scripts are dropped: parity runs JS off on both sides. Nothing else is fetched.*
